clue.text: One's knocked back drink in Scottish island entertainment centre

indicators.note: in places the reversed piece and the drink inside the island's name

parts.note: Mull is an island in the Inner Hebrides

indicators.note: knocked back means the letters of one's are turned round to read backwards

parts.note: one's is I + 'S, i.e. I and S
cha is a slang word for tea

explanation.surface: Someone on a Hebridean island downs a drink at the local entertainment venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking, but it is the reversal signal. Mull is an island in Scotland's Inner Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: A music hall was a Victorian variety theatre, a venue offering popular entertainment.

clue.text: Mother ran into US playwright

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
to run into someone is to meet them, past tense met

explanation.surface: Mum bumped into an American dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: David Mamet is an American dramatist, author of Glengarry Glen Ross.

clue.text: Performer mentioned opening in Asian country

indicators.note: mentioned says the performer's word is to be heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: a singer is a performer
a pore is a tiny opening in the skin

explanation.surface: A performer is cited at a show's opening in some Asian nation.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent singer ends in an 'uh' sound, written SINGA here.
explanation.definitionFit: Singapore is a city-state in Southeast Asia, a sovereign nation.

clue.text: Conservative party upset by Private Eye smarty-pants

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the party word is read backwards

parts.note: a revel is a lively party
dick is old slang for a private detective

explanation.surface: A Tory gathering is upset by a satirical magazine mocking a know-all.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye is a British satirical magazine, but here it is a detective; REVEL upset gives LEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mocking British terms for someone annoyingly keen to show off their intelligence.

clue.text: Generally gutted Arsenal supporter

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving the first and last letters of Arsenal

parts.note: a lover is a fan or supporter of something

explanation.surface: A fan of Arsenal football club is devastated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' reads as British slang for upset, but it strips Arsenal to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Generally and all over both mean everywhere or throughout, as in 'known all over'.

clue.text: Poetic lines sent up in Cilla hit

indicators.note: in puts the reversed lines inside the jumbled singer's name
hit suggests the name is knocked about into a new order
in a down clue sent up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: RY, for railway, gives lines

explanation.surface: Verses parodied in one of Cilla Black's hit songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' is the anagram signal, not a chart success; Cilla Black was a 1960s British pop singer. RY (railway) is a crossword staple for lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrical describes expression with the qualities of poetry or song.

clue.text: Substitute, perhaps, brings about shout of joy

parts.note: Substitute is a 1966 single by The Who, so a work by that band
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A replacement player prompts a joyful cry from the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Substitute looks like a sports bench player; it is a Who song, a Who op(us).
explanation.definitionFit: A whoop is a loud cry of excitement or delight.

clue.text: Architect put in corner window the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way says the hidden letters are read backwards
put in signals letters sitting inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A designer installed a corner window back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Architect put' as definition; 'put in' is the hidden-word signal, leaving 'Architect'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Christopher Wren was the architect of St Paul's Cathedral in London.

clue.text: Pen turned over by one wild beast

indicators.note: turned over means the pen word is flipped to read backwards

parts.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An enclosure is overturned by a single wild animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Pen suggests an animal enclosure, but it is a ballpoint, named after its inventor László Bíró.
explanation.definitionFit: The oribi is a small African antelope, an animal living in the wild.

clue.text: Former champion boxer won't stop talking

definitions.meaning: Floyd ... was world heavyweight champion in the 1950s and 60s
keeps up a stream of glib chatter

explanation.surface: A retired title-holding boxer is a nonstop chatterer.
explanation.definitionFit: Floyd Patterson held the heavyweight title; read as two words, the name means keeps chattering away.

clue.text: Some enthusiasm on team for game

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A little team spirit is needed for a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'for game' takes in the link word 'for'; the definition is just 'game'.
explanation.definitionFit: Monte, or three-card monte, is a gambling card game.

clue.text: Criminal's name appearing in various articles

indicators.note: appearing in places the name's letter inside the rearranged word
various suggests the letters of articles in assorted order

explanation.surface: An offender's name crops up in several newspaper pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal's' is read as 'Criminal is'; N goes into an anagram of ARTICLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who commits larceny, or theft, is a lawbreaker.

clue.text: Set puzzle, with something wrong

parts.note: a teaser is a puzzle or brainteaser
a vice is a wrongdoing or immoral habit

explanation.surface: A puzzle has been set that contains an error.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching collection of cups, saucers and pot is a set of crockery.

clue.text: Fish cook ultimately put in pastry dish

indicators.note: put in places that letter inside the pastry dish

parts.note: a pie is a dish baked in pastry

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of cook

explanation.surface: A chef finally puts fish into a pie.
explanation.definitionFit: The pike is a predatory freshwater fish.

clue.text: Toy bear with stuffing, a great deal

parts.note: padding is soft material used to stuff something
a ton, or tons, means a great deal

explanation.surface: A soft toy bear packed with lots of filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington Bear, from Michael Bond's books, is a famous children's character sold as a cuddly toy.

clue.text: Children given mash, missing starter — soup

indicators.note: missing starter means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to powder something is to crush or mash it

explanation.surface: Kids get mashed food and no first course, only soup.
explanation.walkthrough: Starter suggests a meal's first course, but it is the first letter, P, dropped from POWDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Chowder is a thick soup, often of fish or clams.

clue.text: Tea with a starter of fried rice cooked here?

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are worked up into a new arrangement

parts.note: the word tea with the letter a added alongside it

indicators.note: starter of picks the opening letter of fried

explanation.surface: A place where you might get tea and some fried rice.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'here?', leaning on the rest of the clue: a place where such food is cooked and served.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-service restaurant is a place where tea and simple cooked meals like fried rice are served.

clue.text: People advocating page should be set aside for newspaper articles

indicators.note: set aside means the page letter is removed

parts.note: pleaders are people who argue a case

explanation.surface: Campaigners want a page cleared for opinion columns.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaders are editorials, a newspaper's main opinion pieces.

clue.text: Finance expert misinterpreted emoticons

indicators.note: misinterpreted suggests the letters are read in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A money specialist misread the smiley faces in a message.
explanation.definitionFit: An economist studies money, markets and the wider economy.

clue.text: Wearing warm coat that's ripped off

definitions.meaning: clad in a fleece, a warm fibre jacket
cheated or overcharged, as a sheep is shorn

explanation.surface: A shopper in a warm jacket has been swindled.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece someone is to swindle them; one wearing a fleece jacket is also fleeced.

clue.text: I'm being worn during dates?

indicators.note: during places the middle pieces inside the pair of date letters

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for date, so two of them
I'm being expands to I am
clothes being worn are on

explanation.surface: A ring speaks: it is put on during a courtship.
explanation.walkthrough: Each date gives one D, so the pair frame the middle. Read whole, the clue is the engagement ring talking.
explanation.definitionFit: A diamond engagement ring is the jewel worn by someone in a courting relationship.

clue.text: Live with religious scholar, and have to prepare for rest

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
DD is Doctor of Divinity
to own is to have

explanation.surface: Lodge with a theologian and get ready to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: To bed down is to settle somewhere to sleep for the night.

clue.text: Giant egg served up in no end of gravy

indicators.note: in places the reversed egg inside the shortened gravy
no end of means the gravy word loses its last letter

parts.note: Bisto is a British brand of gravy granules

indicators.note: in a down clue served up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A huge egg dished up in gravy.
explanation.walkthrough: Bisto is a well-known British gravy powder; without its end it gives BIST, around GGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Giant as an adjective means very large, the largest of sizes.

clue.text: Money paid by traveller in Thailand — over two pounds

parts.note: T is the international vehicle code for Thailand
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for over
L is the abbreviation for pound, so two of them

explanation.surface: A traveller in Thailand pays a fee of just over two pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A toll is a charge levied for using a road or bridge.

clue.text: Extreme Liberal, that's me

parts.note: said in a game of tag or when picked: I'm it

explanation.surface: A politician declares himself the most extreme Liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: The limit is the furthest or extreme point, beyond which one cannot go.

clue.text: Enjoying oneself producing anti-capital punishment slogan

definitions.meaning: a protest chant calling for the gallows to be abolished

explanation.surface: Having fun while chanting against executions.
explanation.definitionFit: Spending leisure time casually; read as a slogan, it calls for an end to execution by the rope.

clue.text: Fashion garment at bottom has tear

indicators.note: in a down clue, the garment has the next piece below it

parts.note: T stands for a T-shirt
to rend is to tear

explanation.surface: A fashion item has a rip at the hem.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend is a general fashion or direction of popular taste.

clue.text: Bridge partners wanting a quiet game of cards

parts.note: in bridge South and North play as partners
P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Bridge players want a peaceful round of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Snap is a simple children's card game where matching cards are called.

clue.text: Distinguishing feature of country garden ultimately covered in bloom

indicators.note: covered in puts the country and letter inside the flower

parts.note: a rose is a flower, or bloom
Oman is a country in Arabia

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of garden

explanation.surface: A country garden is distinguished by being covered in flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A prominent aquiline nose is a distinctive facial characteristic.

clue.text: Hallucinogenic experience with drug? Nonsense

parts.note: a trip is the effect of taking LSD
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Taking another drug on top of an acid trip is ridiculous.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe, literally cow stomach, is slang for rubbish or worthless talk.

clue.text: Behave badly in a court before the judge

parts.note: to be up is to appear in court

explanation.surface: Misbehaving in a courtroom in front of the judge.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to misbehave or show off.

clue.text: Blasted school in old-fashioned setting

indicators.note: setting means holding something within, as a ring sets a gem

parts.note: dated means out of fashion
Eton is the English public school

explanation.surface: A school in an antiquated setting was blown up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' reads as surroundings but is the container signal, holding the school as a mount holds a gem; Eton is the famous English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Detonated means exploded, as a bomb is blasted.
